goal: Unify current CPU and GPU profile producers behind one TLS-based structured dump interface that supports file and TCP output, uses compile-time validated schema templates, exposes DUMP_STREAM(template) << ... syntax, provides explicit TLS flush entry points, and locks its startup configuration through readonly-after-startup CVars.

how_they_apply_here: Do not keep both FlameProfiler JSON save and Trace packet streaming as separate first-class output interfaces after the unified dump stream lands. CPU and GPU profile export must converge on one producer-facing interface.
Do not build a generic telemetry framework. Keep the design narrow: one profile dump hub, one TLS producer path, one structured schema model, and two concrete sinks only: file and TCP.
Validation must stay on existing repository scripts. If focused coverage is missing, add test cases to existing test targets instead of adding a new profiler-specific top-level script.
Validation acceptance only cares about functional failure and validation errors. Warnings are not a reason to complicate the design.
All scripted validation examples in this checkpoint use PowerShell on Windows.

rules_used: Reject useless wrappers and pass-through layers.
Validate only with existing repository scripts.
Keep ownership explicit and control flow direct.
how_they_apply_here: The design must converge CPU and GPU profile data into one latest-only dump interface instead of adding a third export path beside existing ones.
The public API must be direct. DUMP_STREAM(template) writes into the real owner; it must not be a cosmetic wrapper over multiple hidden subsystems.
Producer ownership, TLS shard ownership, and sink ownership must be explicit in the design document.
Testing strategy must stay on current scripts only.

already_exists: CPU profile collection already uses thread_local stack state in FlameProfiler for scope nesting and collects events into a global vector.
GPU profile events already resolve into structured queue scopes through GPUEventStream and are emitted into the Trace runtime.
Trace runtime already supports TCP streaming and CSV/file output and is initialized from Editor with host/port configuration.
MoerProfiler already consumes streamed trace data over TCP in the current architecture.
gaps: CPU flame export and GPU trace export do not share one producer-facing structured schema contract today.
Current CPU profile save path is ad-hoc JSON serialization and is not compile-time schema checked.
Current Trace API is structured, but it is not exposed as a compile-time templated DUMP_STREAM contract with field-type sequencing guarantees.
There is no unified TLS-backed producer API that both CPU and GPU profile producers use to write records into one sink pipeline.
There is no explicit TLS flush control or startup-readonly cache tuning for one unified profile dump path today.

hard_constraints.title: One producer-facing interface only
hard_constraints.detail: CPU and GPU profiling producers must converge on one structured dump write interface. Do not keep separate long-term producer APIs for FlameProfiler JSON save and Trace packet streaming.

hard_constraints.title: TLS write path on hot path
hard_constraints.detail: Producer-side writes must go into thread-local shards or thread-local staging buffers so common CPU/GPU profile emission does not contend on one global mutex per record.

hard_constraints.title: Compile-time schema validation
hard_constraints.detail: Template definition must encode channel type, record type, and ordered field types in a way that wrong field type, wrong field count, or incomplete << chain fails at compile time.

hard_constraints.title: Exactly two sink kinds in first landing
hard_constraints.detail: The first design supports file sink and TCP sink only. Do not introduce a generic plugin sink registry or speculative extensibility surface.

hard_constraints.title: Structured output format
hard_constraints.detail: The unified stream must define a schema packet plus record packet contract, or an equivalent explicitly versioned structured format, so file output and network output carry the same semantic record model.

hard_constraints.title: Validation stays on existing scripts
hard_constraints.detail: Implementation validation must use existing PowerShell scripts only. If profiler-specific coverage is missing, extend existing test targets and route them through current scripts instead of creating a new top-level profiler script.

hard_constraints.title: Explicit TLS flush is part of the contract
hard_constraints.detail: The unified profile dump path must expose an explicit TLS flush entry point for current-thread shard publication and immediate sink visibility in special cases.

hard_constraints.title: TLS cache tuning is startup-only readonly config
hard_constraints.detail: TLS shard capacity and auto-publish thresholds must have code defaults and startup override CVars that become runtime read-only after startup config application.

ownership_model.ProfileDumpHub: Single process-level owner of schema registry, sink configuration, TLS shard registration, chunk ingestion, and final sink write ordering.
ownership_model.ProfileDumpTlsShard: One thread_local append-only record buffer per producer thread. Producers write fully typed records here with no per-record global lock.
ownership_model.ProfileDumpDrain: One explicit drain path that moves completed TLS chunks into the hub and pushes them to configured sinks in deterministic order.
ownership_model.ProfileDumpSink: Two concrete sink implementations only in first landing: TcpProfileDumpSink and FileProfileDumpSink.

public_api.template_macro: Define one macro family that declares a dump template type containing dump category, channel type, schema name, version, and ordered field types.
flush_api: ProfileDump::FlushThreadLocal() publishes the current thread TLS shard and drains published records to sinks.
ProfileDump::FlushAll() drains all already-published records to sinks and is used by frame-end or shutdown code paths.
ProfileDump::Shutdown() performs final drain and closes file/TCP sinks.
required_semantics: DUMP_STREAM(template) returns a move-only compile-time builder typed by template and current field index.
Each operator<< only accepts the exact next field type or a whitelisted convertible type defined by explicit dump traits.
The final builder stage commits the record into the TLS shard automatically.
Incomplete stream usage is surfaced as a compile-time nodiscard contract and wrong type / wrong extra operand remain compile-time errors.
compile_time_guarantees: Wrong operand type for a field fails compilation.
Template channel type is part of the type identity and cannot be changed at call site.
Only explicitly supported field types are legal in templates.

field_type_policy: Allow only a narrow approved set in first landing: bool, fixed-width integers, float, double, enum class with explicit underlying type, and string_view-like non-owning text with explicit serialization traits.
Reject arbitrary STL containers, variant trees, and nested dynamic objects in first landing.
Schema id should be deterministic from template metadata so file and TCP sinks serialize the same record family consistently.

required_behavior: Producers append typed records into thread_local shard storage.
Shard rollover publishes immutable chunks to the central hub.
The hub serializes chunk order per shard and then emits to file and/or TCP sinks.
Drain points must be explicit; thread teardown only performs best-effort shard handoff and does not replace explicit flush points.
preferred_flush_points: End-of-frame on the main thread for regular runtime draining.
Explicit FlushThreadLocal() for special dumps or current-thread visibility requirements.
Thread teardown for best-effort final shard handoff.
Explicit Stop/Shutdown path for final sink flush.
non_goals: No remote command channel back from profiler to editor in first landing.

file_sink: Writes the same structured packet model used by TCP sink, not a separate ad-hoc JSON export format.
File output is append-only within one session and explicitly finalized on shutdown or stop.
tcp_sink: Reuses the current one-way editor-to-profiler direction.
Schema packets are sent before first record packet for a schema id.
Do not introduce bidirectional control messages in first landing.
sink_model.configuration_rule: The unified dump hub may enable file sink, TCP sink, or both from one config object. Producer code does not know which sink combination is active.
startup_readonly_config: Profile.Dump.FileEnabled, Profile.Dump.TcpEnabled, Profile.Dump.FilePath, Profile.Dump.TcpHost, and Profile.Dump.TcpPort are startup-readonly CVars.
Profile.Dump.TlsMaxRecords, Profile.Dump.TlsMaxBytes, Profile.Dump.AutoPublishRecords, and Profile.Dump.AutoPublishBytes are startup-readonly CVars.
ConfigManager applies ConsoleVariable.toml overrides first, then seals startup-readonly CVars so runtime console mutation is rejected.

cpu_profile: FlameProfiler stops being a special-case JSON exporter in the target design.
CPU scope begin/end data is normalized into unified dump templates and written through the same TLS stream as other profile records.
gpu_profile: GPUEventStream resolved nodes or equivalent GPU trace output must emit unified dump records through the same hub instead of bypassing it with a separate export path.
GPU queue/channel identity stays explicit in schema/channel metadata.
trace_runtime: Current Trace runtime packet writer becomes one sink/backend implementation detail of the unified profile dump contract, not a parallel user-facing API.
Counter and instant-style profile records may remain supported, but only through the same schema-checked interface.

template_definition_shape: One macro defines a template type with a fixed channel and ordered field list.
Example intent only: CPU scope template carries thread id, name, start_ns, end_ns, depth.
Example intent only: GPU queue scope template carries queue type, frame index, start_ns, end_ns, total_busy_ns, exclusive_ns.
stream_usage_shape: DUMP_STREAM(CpuScopeTemplate) << thread_id << name << start_ns << end_ns << depth;
Wrong field type and extra stream operands are compile-time failures by design.
compile_time_rejection_examples: Passing float to a uint64 field must fail compilation.
Stopping after fewer << operands than the template field count must fail compilation.

checkpoints.title: Define the schema-checked dump template contract
must_be_true_after: One template macro family defines dump type, channel type, schema version, and ordered field types.
DUMP_STREAM(template) << ... becomes the only producer-facing write shape for the new interface.
FlushThreadLocal and FlushAll exist as explicit drain controls.
TLS shard capacity and auto-publish thresholds have startup-readonly defaults plus ConsoleVariable.toml override support.
Wrong field type, wrong field count, and incomplete stream use are compile-time failures by design.
Only explicitly supported field types are legal in first landing.

files_likely_affected.title: Land one TLS aggregation path and two concrete sinks
must_be_true_after: Producer writes go through thread_local shard storage instead of per-record global locking.
The process owns one ProfileDumpHub that drains TLS chunks and writes structured packets.
File sink and TCP sink use the same packet and schema model.
Producer code does not branch on file-versus-network destination.
Existing trace emission may remain temporarily for editor profiler continuity, but unified CPU/GPU dump export now goes through the new stream.

files_likely_affected.title: Move CPU and GPU profile producers onto the unified stream
must_be_true_after: CPU flame profile records are emitted through the unified dump stream instead of a special-case JSON save path.
GPU resolved scope/profile records are emitted through the same unified dump stream with explicit GPU channel metadata.
There are focused compile-time and runtime tests for template type checking, startup-readonly cvar sealing, explicit TLS flush, file sink serialization, and GPU producer integration.
Producer code does not branch on file-versus-network destination.

files_likely_affected.title: Validate with existing scripts and focused test cases only
must_be_true_after: There are focused compile-time and runtime tests for template type checking, field-count checking, TLS chunk drain, file sink serialization, and TCP packet/schema ordering.
If no dedicated profiler script exists, these tests are added to existing test targets and executed through current repository PowerShell scripts instead of a new top-level script.
Focused validation runs powershell -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File .\testscripts\test_rhi_translate.ps1 first if the new tests live in the existing core/RHI test path.
Broader regression validation runs powershell -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File .\testscripts\test_all.ps1 after focused validation passes, and validation acceptance only cares about errors.

rejected_alternatives.name: Keep FlameProfiler JSON save and add unified stream beside it
rejected_alternatives.reason: This keeps compatibility duplication and violates the latest-only convergence rule.

rejected_alternatives.name: Build a generic telemetry framework with arbitrary sink plugins
rejected_alternatives.reason: The task is narrower than that and Rule_Codex forbids over-design here.

rejected_alternatives.name: Use one global mutex-protected vector for all producer writes
rejected_alternatives.reason: The user explicitly wants a TLS-based aggregation path and the hot path should not serialize all producer threads behind one lock.

rejected_alternatives.name: Allow runtime field-type checking instead of compile-time checking
rejected_alternatives.reason: The requested interface requires compile-time validation of the structured output contract.

validation: Planning only in this checkpoint. No implementation is part of this file.
When implementation starts, do not add a new standalone profiler top-level script.
Add focused tests to existing covered test targets, then run powershell -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File .\testscripts\test_rhi_translate.ps1 if those tests land in the current RHI/core test path.
After focused tests pass, run powershell -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File .\testscripts\test_all.ps1.

If editor/profiler runtime smoke coverage is needed later, use powershell -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File .\testscripts\test_editor.ps1 or extend existing aggregate coverage instead of introducing a new primary profiler script.
